title: League of Legends Launched With a Subtitle Nobody Remembers
hook: Riot announced its first game on October 7, 2008 as League of Legends: Clash of Fates. The subtitle was gone by the October 27, 2009 launch, and this week Riot teased a 2027 overhaul called New Dawn. What was the first champion you ever played?
script: Did you know League of Legends launched with a subtitle almost nobody remembers? On October 7th, 2008, a two year old studio called Riot Games announced its very first game. The press called it League of Legends: Clash of Fates. Riot had been founded in 2006, and part of its team had worked on DotA Allstars, the Warcraft 3 mod that pioneered the genre. The pitch was a standalone version of that idea with dozens of champions and more than two hundred items. In July 2009 Riot confirmed something that was unusual at the time. The whole game would be free, with optional Riot Points you could buy with real money. By the time it launched on October 27th, 2009, the Clash of Fates subtitle was gone and the game shipped with about forty champions. Seventeen years later it is still going. This week League is in the news again. During the Worlds final on November 14th, Riot teased League of Legends: New Dawn, an overhaul coming in 2027. It promises a modernized client, a redrawn Summoner's Rift and new ways to play each champion. A full reveal is planned for January. What was the first champion you ever played? Follow for more gaming history.
